title: Your Stomach Acid Can Dissolve Metal
fact: Gastric acid in your stomach has a pH of 1-2, which is strong enough to dissolve some metals. It can break down food and kill bacteria that enter your digestive system.

title: The Sun Is 93 Million Miles Away
fact: The Sun is approximately 93 million miles (150 million km) from Earth. Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach us.

title: Crocodiles Can't Stick Their Tongue Out
fact: A crocodile's tongue is held in place by a membrane and cannot move. However, they have salt glands on their tongues to help excrete excess salt from seawater.

title: The Longest River in Europe Is 3,530 km
fact: The Volga River in Russia is the longest river in Europe, stretching 3,530 kilometers. It flows into the Caspian Sea and drains about one-third of European Russia.

title: A Byte Contains 8 Bits
fact: A byte is the basic unit of digital information, consisting of 8 bits. Each bit can be either 0 or 1, giving 256 possible combinations per byte.

title: Forests Cover 31% of Global Land Area
fact: Forests cover approximately 31% of the world's land area, providing habitat for 80% of terrestrial biodiversity. They also store about 45% of carbon stored on land.

title: Paper Was Invented in China Around 100 CE
fact: Cai Lun invented paper in China around 100 CE, using bark, hemp, and rags. This invention revolutionized communication and record-keeping worldwide.

title: Owls Can Rotate Their Heads 270 Degrees
fact: Owls have flexible necks that allow them to rotate their heads up to 270 degrees. This compensates for their fixed eyeballs that cannot move in their sockets.

title: The Universe Is 13.8 Billion Years Old
fact: The universe began with the Big Bang approximately 13.8 billion years ago. The oldest light we can see comes from about 380,000 years after this event.

title: Your DNA Would Stretch to Pluto and Back
fact: If you uncoiled all the DNA in your body and stretched it out, it would reach about 10 billion miles, enough to go to Pluto and back twice.

title: Mount Kilimanjaro Is a Volcano
fact: Mount Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano in Tanzania with three volcanic cones: Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira. It is the highest mountain in Africa at 5,895 meters.

title: Bees Can Recognize Human Faces
fact: Honeybees can recognize and remember human faces using a method called configural processing, similar to how humans recognize faces.

title: The First Web Browser Was Created in 1990
fact: Tim Berners-Lee created the first web browser called WorldWideWeb in 1990 at CERN. It was later renamed Nexus to avoid confusion with the web itself.

title: The Amazon River Has 3,000 Species of Fish
fact: The Amazon River basin contains approximately 3,000 known species of fish, with many more yet to be discovered. This is more fish species than in the entire Atlantic Ocean.

title: The Pyramids Were Built by Paid Workers
fact: Recent evidence shows the Great Pyramids were built by paid workers, not slaves. These workers were well-fed and received medical care, and were buried in tombs near the pyramids.

title: Starfish Have Blue Blood
fact: Starfish have pale blue blood due to hemocyanin containing copper, instead of iron-based hemoglobin. This is more efficient in cold, low-oxygen environments.

title: Your Brain Is 73% Water
fact: The human brain is composed of approximately 73% water. Even slight dehydration can affect cognitive function, mood, and concentration.

title: Iceland Has No Mosquitoes
fact: Iceland is one of few countries with no native mosquito species. Scientists believe the country's harsh climate cycles of freezing and thawing prevent mosquito larvae from surviving.

title: Elephants Use seismic Communication
fact: Elephants can communicate through seismic vibrations that travel through the ground. They use special sensors in their feet and trunk to detect these signals.

title: USB Stands for Universal Serial Bus
fact: USB was developed in the mid-1990s by Intel, Microsoft, Compaq, and others to standardize computer connections. The USB 1.0 could transfer data at 12 Mbps.

title: Coral Reefs Support 25% of Marine Life
fact: Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor but support about 25% of all marine species. They are often called the 'rainforests of the sea.'

title: The Great Fire of London Burned 13,200 Houses
fact: The Great Fire of London in 1666 destroyed 13,200 houses, 87 churches, and St. Paul's Cathedral. It killed about 70,000 people and burned for 4 days.

title: Frogs Don't Drink Water Through Their Mouths
fact: Frogs absorb water through a 'drinking patch' on their belly called the ventral skin. They also absorb moisture and breathe through their skin.

title: The Largest Galaxy Has 100 Trillion Stars
fact: IC 1101 is the largest known galaxy, containing over 100 trillion stars. It is about 6 million light-years in diameter, compared to the Milky Way's 100,000 light-years.

title: Your Body Has About 60,000 Miles of Blood Vessels
fact: If all your blood vessels were laid end to end, they would stretch about 60,000 miles. This is enough to circle the Earth more than twice.

title: The Pacific Ocean Covers 63 Million Square Miles
fact: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about 63 million square miles. It is larger than all the land on Earth combined.

title: Seahorses Travel Upright
fact: Seahorses are the only fish species that swim upright. They use their dorsal fin for propulsion and steer with tiny pectoral fins on their sides.

title: The First Computer Mouse Was Made of Wood
fact: Doug Engelbart invented the first computer mouse in 1964, which was made of wood with two wheels. It took nearly 20 years before it became commercially available.

title: Some Trees Can Live for Thousands of Years
fact: Bristlecone pine trees in the USA are among the oldest living organisms, with some individuals exceeding 5,000 years. Their dead wood often remains standing for centuries.

title: The Berlin Wall Stood for 28 Years
fact: The Berlin Wall was built in 1961 and fell in 1989, dividing East and West Berlin for 28 years. Over 100 people died trying to cross it.

title: Snakes Can Feel Love
fact: Recent research suggests snakes can form bonds with humans and recognize their owners. They may show preference for familiar people and experience stress when separated.

title: Jupiter Has 95 Known Moons
fact: Jupiter has 95 known moons as of 2023, the most of any planet in our solar system. The four largest are the Galilean moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.

title: You Blink About 15-20 Times Per Minute
fact: On average, you blink 15-20 times per minute, or about 1,200 times per hour. Each blink lasts 0.1-0.4 seconds, totaling about 23 minutes of blinking daily.

title: The Mariana Trench Is 36,070 Feet Deep
fact: The Mariana Trench is the deepest part of the ocean, reaching 36,070 feet (10,994 meters). Mount Everest would fit inside with over a mile to spare.

title: Koalas Have Fingerprints Like Humans
fact: Koalas have fingerprints that are almost indistinguishable from human fingerprints under a microscope. This can cause confusion at crime scenes.

title: The First Programmer Was a Woman
fact: Ada Lovelace, writing in the 1840s, created the first algorithm intended for a machine. She is considered the first computer programmer.

title: Forests Can Create Their Own Climate
fact: Large forests create their own microclimates through transpiration, releasing massive amounts of water vapor that can form clouds and trigger rainfall.

title: Shakespeare Invented 1,700 Words
fact: William Shakespeare is credited with inventing about 1,700 words used in the English language, including 'assassination', 'bedroom', and 'lonely'.

title: Butterflies Have Compound Eyes
fact: A butterfly's compound eye contains thousands of lenses, giving it nearly 360-degree vision. However, they see far fewer colors than humans.

title: The Nearest Star Is 4.24 Light-Years Away
fact: Proxima Centauri is the closest star to our Sun at 4.24 light-years distance. At current spacecraft speeds, it would take about 73,000 years to reach it.

title: Your Brain Uses 20% of Your Oxygen
fact: Despite being only 2% of body weight, the brain uses 20% of the body's oxygen supply. This makes it extremely vulnerable to oxygen deprivation.

title: The Amazon Rainforest Is 5.5 Million km²
fact: The Amazon rainforest covers about 5.5 million square kilometers, spanning nine countries. It is the largest tropical rainforest in the world.

title: Camels Have Three Eyelids
fact: Camels have three eyelids to protect their eyes from sand and dust. Two of the eyelids have lashes, and one is transparent to see through while protecting the eye.

title: The First Camera Weighed 50 Pounds
fact: Joseph Nicéphore Niépce created the first camera in 1826, which weighed about 50 pounds and required an 8-hour exposure time to capture an image.

title: Trees Absorb More CO2 Than They Release
fact: Trees absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis and release oxygen. A mature tree can absorb about 48 pounds of CO2 per year and produce 260 pounds of oxygen.

title: The Titanic Had 20 Lifeboats, Needed 48
fact: The Titanic carried only 20 lifeboats, enough for about half the people aboard. Maritime regulations at the time did not require more.

title: Goldfish Have a Memory Span of 3 Months
fact: Goldfish can remember things for at least 3 months, contrary to the popular myth of 3 seconds. They can be trained to respond to colors and sounds.

title: Uranus Orbits the Sun on Its Side
fact: Uranus has an axial tilt of 98 degrees, essentially orbiting the Sun on its side. This was likely caused by a collision with an Earth-sized object long ago.

title: Your Lungs Contain 300 Million Alveoli
fact: Your lungs contain about 300 million tiny air sacs called alveoli. If spread flat, they would cover about 70 square meters, roughly half a tennis court.

title: The Grand Canyon Is 277 Miles Long
fact: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is 277 miles long, up to 18 miles wide, and over a mile deep. It was formed by the Colorado River over 5-6 million years.

title: Sloths Can Hold Their Breath for 40 Minutes
fact: Sloths can hold their breath for up to 40 minutes, which is longer than dolphins. This ability helps them avoid predators and survive underwater.

title: The First Smartphone Was Called Simon
fact: IBM's Simon Personal Communicator, released in 1994, is considered the first smartphone. It combined a mobile phone with a PDA and cost $899.

title: The Amazon Emits Less CO2 Than It Absorbs
fact: The Amazon rainforest absorbs more carbon dioxide than it emits, acting as a major carbon sink. It stores about 100-150 billion metric tons of carbon.

title: The Black Death Killed 30-60% of Europe's Population
fact: The Black Death (1347-1351) killed an estimated 75-200 million people in Eurasia, reducing Europe's population by 30-60% in just a few years.

title: Ostriches Can Run Faster Than Horses
fact: Ostriches can run at speeds up to 45 mph (72 km/h), faster than horses which max out at about 30 mph. They are the fastest two-legged animals on land.

title: Neutron Stars Are 12 Miles Wide but Weigh More Than the Sun
fact: Neutron stars pack the mass of about 1.4 suns into a sphere only 12 miles (20 km) across. A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh billions of tons.

title: Your Skin Weighs About 8 Pounds
fact: The skin is the largest organ in the human body, weighing about 8 pounds (3.6 kg) in adults. It covers about 20 square feet in average adults.

title: Lake Vostok Has Been Sealed for 15 Million Years
fact: Lake Vostok in Antarctica has been isolated from the rest of the world for about 15 million years. It may contain unique forms of life never seen before.

title: Pigeons Can Do Math
fact: Research has shown that pigeons can learn to rank objects by abstract numerical concepts, demonstrating mathematical abilities previously thought to be unique to primates.

title: The First Email Was Sent in 1971
fact: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971, using the @ sign to separate the user name from the computer name. He also chose QWERTYUIOP as the first message.

title: Forests Can Be Named After Colors
fact: Some forests are named after their autumn colors, like Japan's 'momiji' (maple) forests that turn brilliant red. Different trees produce different color pigments.

title: The French Revolution Began in 1789
fact: The French Revolution began on July 14, 1789, with the storming of the Bastille. It led to the end of the monarchy and the rise of Napoleon Bonaparte.

title: Sharks Have No Bones
fact: Sharks are made entirely of cartilage, the same flexible material in human noses and ears. Their skeletons are much lighter, helping them stay buoyant.

title: There Are More Galaxies Than Stars in the Observable Universe
fact: The observable universe contains an estimated 200 billion galaxies, each with 100-400 billion stars. No one knows how many galaxies exist beyond our observable universe.

title: Your Brain Stops Feeling Hungry When Full
fact: The hormone ghrelin stimulates hunger, while leptin signals fullness. Your stomach produces ghrelin, and fat cells produce leptin to regulate appetite.

title: There Are 195 Countries in the World
fact: There are 195 countries in the world: 193 are member states of the United Nations, plus 2 observer states (Vatican City and Palestine).

title: Parrots Can Learn to Use Tools
fact: Some parrots, like the kea of New Zealand, have been observed using tools and solving complex problems. They can also learn to use objects as implements.

title: The First Computer Virus Was Created in 1971
fact: The Creeper virus, created by Bob Thomas in 1971, was the first computer virus. It displayed the message 'I'm the Creeper: Catch me if you can!'

title: Trees Can Absorb Sound Pollution
fact: Dense vegetation can reduce noise pollution by absorbing and deflecting sound waves. A row of trees can reduce noise by 6-8 decibels per 30 meters.

title: The Industrial Revolution Changed Work Permanently
fact: The Industrial Revolution (1760-1840) transformed society from agricultural to industrial, introducing factories, mass production, and wage labor.

title: Salamanders Can Regrow Lost Limbs
fact: Salamanders can regrow entire limbs, parts of their heart, liver, lungs, brain, and spinal cord. Scientists study them to understand how to trigger similar regeneration in humans.

title: The Sun Makes Up 99.86% of the Solar System's Mass
fact: The Sun contains 99.86% of all the mass in the solar system. Jupiter alone makes up most of the remaining 0.14%.

title: Your Brain Uses Electricity
fact: The human brain generates about 20 watts of electrical power, enough to power a small light bulb. Neurons fire at speeds up to 268 mph.

title: The Mediterranean Sea Is Almost Completely Surrounded by Land
fact: The Mediterranean Sea is connected to the Atlantic Ocean only by the 8.9-mile-wide Strait of Gibraltar. It is almost entirely enclosed by Europe, Asia, and Africa.

title: Some Jellyfish Are Immortal
fact: Turritopsis dohrnii, the 'immortal jellyfish,' can revert to its juvenile polyp stage after reaching maturity, theoretically living forever under ideal conditions.

title: HTTPS Uses Encryption for Security
fact: HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) uses SSL/TLS encryption to protect data transmitted between browsers and servers, making online transactions safer.

title: Some Trees Can Communicate Through Root Systems
fact: Trees in forests are connected by mycorrhizal fungi networks, allowing them to share nutrients and send chemical signals to warn of insect attacks.

title: The Roman Empire Lasted Over 500 Years
fact: The Roman Empire lasted from 27 BCE to 476 CE, a span of over 500 years. At its height, it controlled about 5 million square kilometers.

title: Bats Are the Only Mammals Capable of Sustained Flight
fact: While flying squirrels glide, bats are the only mammals that can truly fly. Their wings are made of a membrane stretched over elongated finger bones.

title: The Moon Is Slowly Moving Away from Earth
fact: The Moon recedes from Earth at about 3.8 centimeters per year. In 600 million years, it will be too far away to completely cover the Sun during eclipses.

title: You Produce 25,000 Quarts of Saliva in a Lifetime
fact: The average person produces about 0.7 liters of saliva per day, totaling about 25,000 quarts over a lifetime. Saliva contains enzymes that begin digestion.

title: Mount Everest Is Getting Taller
fact: Mount Everest grows about 4 millimeters taller every year due to the collision of the Indian and Asian tectonic plates, which continues to push the Himalayas upward.

title: Cows Can Walk Upstairs but Not Down
fact: Cows can walk upstairs but struggle to walk downstairs because of the angle of their knees and their heavy front ends. This is why they rarely go down steep slopes.

title: QR Codes Can Store Up to 2,900 Bytes
fact: QR codes can store up to 2,953 bytes of data, which translates to about 4,296 alphanumeric characters. They use error correction to remain readable when partially damaged.

title: Forests Can Reduce Air Temperature
fact: Trees can reduce ambient air temperature by up to 10 degrees Fahrenheit through shade and transpiration. A single tree can have the cooling effect of 10 room-sized air conditioners.

title: The First Wheel Was Used 5,500 Years Ago
fact: The earliest known wheels date to about 3500 BCE in Mesopotamia. They were initially used for pottery before being adapted for transportation.

title: A Whale's Heart Beats Only 4-8 Times Per Minute
fact: A blue whale's heart is the size of a small car and beats only 4-8 times per minute. Its heartbeat can be detected from 2 miles away underwater.

title: Light Takes 8 Minutes to Travel from Sun to Earth
fact: Light travels at 186,000 miles per second and takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth from the Sun. The Sun is 93 million miles away.

title: Your Hair Grows About 6 Inches Per Year
fact: On average, human hair grows about 6 inches (15 cm) per year, or about 0.3-0.4 mm per day. Hair grows faster in summer than winter.

title: Australia Is Both a Country and a Continent
fact: Australia is the smallest continent and largest island, as well as being the only continent that is also a single country. It covers about 7.7 million km².

title: Sea Otters Hold Hands While Sleeping
fact: Sea otters often hold paws while sleeping to prevent drifting apart. They also wrap themselves in kelp to anchor themselves in place.

title: The Internet Has 4.5 Billion Users
fact: As of 2023, about 4.5 billion people use the internet, representing about 59% of the global population. This number continues to grow every year.

title: Forests Can Take 100+ Years to Mature
fact: Old-growth forests take over 100 years to develop their complex ecosystems. These forests contain the most biodiversity and store the most carbon.

title: The Printing Press Was Invented in 1440
fact: Johannes Gutenberg invented the printing press around 1440, revolutionizing book production. The Gutenberg Bible was the first major book printed with movable type.

title: Penguins Propose with Pebbles
fact: Male Adelie penguins propose to females by presenting them with carefully selected pebbles. If the female accepts, she adds it to their nest.

title: The Universe Has No Center
fact: The universe has no center because it is expanding uniformly in all directions from every point. There is no special location from which to measure expansion.

title: Your Brain Has 86 Billion Neurons
fact: The human brain contains approximately 86 billion neurons, each connected to thousands of others via synapses. This creates a network of about 100 trillion connections.

title: The Dead Sea Is the Lowest Point on Earth
fact: The Dead Sea shoreline is the lowest exposed point on Earth's surface at 430.5 meters below sea level. It is also one of the saltiest bodies of water.

title: Ants Can Carry 50 Times Their Body Weight
fact: Ants can carry objects up to 50 times their own body weight due to their strength-to-weight ratio. This is like a human carrying a car.
